headline: Canadiens’ Chris Kreider out 6-8 weeks with lower-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Montreal forward Chris Kreider will be out 6-8 weeks with a lower-body injury. He has three goals and nine points in 19 games with the Canadiens in 2026-27.

The loss is smaller than the name suggests. Kreider has played third-line minutes (13:35 a night counting all situations), and his own expected goals, which measure the quality of his chances, are 3.62 against his three actual goals, so he has been a bit unlucky rather than hot. At five-on-five Montreal has taken only 42% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and the team's share is 11.7 percentage points better when he sits. The Canadiens are 12-3-4, helped by goals saved above expected of 8.9, a measure of how many goals their goaltending has stopped beyond what the shot quality predicted. We'd say that, more than any one skater, is what to watch. The Hockey News's Karine Hains posted that Florian Xhekaj is in for Kreider tonight. Going by how the coach has used his players, Oliver Kapanen (10:58 a night) is next in line for Kreider's minutes, and the second power-play unit is where we'd look for a change.
